requirement:
Give `search_structure` the language, an ast-grep rule, and an optional match limit. Each match carries a node reference for `read_node` and a tag for `finish_search`.
For the `instructions` field, see {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`.

```text
search_structure({language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer})
  -> {search_id: UUID, instructions?: string, next?: UUID, complete: boolean, matches: {tag: string, node: string, excerpt: string}[]}
```
rationale:
I found no structural gap in the `search_structure` signature or result shape. This check was structural only. I did not run any behavior and did not assess tests.

**Input signature `{language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer}`**
- The `search_structure` entry in `project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` declares an object schema. It has `language` as a string, `rule` as an object, and `limit` as an integer with minimum 0.
- `required` lists only `language` and `rule`, so `limit` is optional, as the requirement says.
- In `project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[dispatch]`, the `"search_structure"` arm requires `rule` to be an object. It reads `language` as a string through the `string` helper. It reads `limit` through `optional_number`, which accepts a missing value or a nonnegative integer. It then builds a `StructuralQuery` with that limit and calls `search_structure`.

**Output shape `{search_id, instructions?, next?, complete, matches: {tag, node, excerpt}[]}`**
- The `"search_structure"` arm in `fn[dispatch]` builds each entry as `{"node": <registered node reference>, "excerpt": <redacted span>}`. The node reference comes from `pages.register`, which is what `read_node` takes. Each entry carries a `Dependency::Node` as its observation.
- `agent/pages.rs#impl[Pages<N, L>]/fn[search]` builds each page as `{search_id: UUID, complete, matches}`. It adds a `tag` to every entry, numbered from "1". Each tag is stored in the page's `entries` map, which is what `finish_search` consumes.
- `fn[search]` adds an `instructions` string only when `first_search && index == 0`. So it appears on the first page of the first search and is omitted on continuation pages and later searches, matching `instructions?`. The wording and delivery rules of `instructions` are the cited requirement's concern, so I did not judge them here.
- `fn[search]` sets `next` to the UUID of the following page. Pages are built in reverse so each page can name its successor. That matches `next?: UUID`.
- `complete` comes from the search results, as a boolean.

**Delegated and cited material**
- The tool `description` is a refining declaration, `search_structure.mcp.description`. I did not assess it here.
- The `first_search.instructions` requirement is cited context only.

The `{impl}` markers on `fn[search]` and `fn[dispatch]` for `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_structure.mcp` match code that does implement the schema and result shape. There are no {fixme} acknowledgments, and none are needed.

text: Give `search_structure` the language, an ast-grep rule, and an optional match limit. Each match carries a node reference for `read_node` and a tag for `finish_search`.
search_structure({language: string, rule: object, limit?: integer})
-> {search_id: UUID, instructions?: string, next?: UUID, complete: boolean, matches: {tag: string, node: string, excerpt: string}[]}
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Find structural matches in available files. Read selected nodes separately.`
